title: Eka Robotics Raises $150M at $1.45B Valuation for Physical AI
summary:
a16z led a new investment in a startup developing robots capable of complex dexterity to reduce reliance on human labor. Eka Robotics secured $150M in Series A funding at a $1.45B post-money valuation to scale its Vision-Force-Action model and accelerate customer deployments. The company claims the new architecture eliminates the traditional trade-off between the general versatility of a robot and its performance in the field.

Co-founders Pulkit Agrawal and Tuomas Haarnoja brought expertise from MIT CSAIL and Google DeepMind to build a system that integrates visual perception with force feedback from robotic hands. This approach enables robots to treat physical contact as information, meaning experience can scale with compute instead of human labor. a16z noted that the solution targets the variable environments of the physical economy that have historically made manual work difficult to automate.

@EkaRobotics has raised a $150M Series A.

Generality v/s Performance is the fundamental tension at the frontier of robotics. Generality without performance is just a prototype. Performance without generality is just a single-purpose tool.

Customers shouldn’t have to choose. Eka breaks the tradeoff. Powered by our Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model, we deliver the performance and versatility customers need to put robots to work every day.

Eka is built on three convictions: 
⚡️Force is the language of manipulation. 
 🚀 Reinforcement learning is how dexterous manipulation scales. 
🎂 System 1—fast, reliable physical execution—is the bottleneck to solve.

With this funding, we will scale our model and accelerate customer deployments.

Grateful to be building alongside a dream team and investors who share our ambition.

selectedTweets.text:
We believe solving dexterous manipulation is one of the largest opportunities in robotics. That’s why we're thrilled to lead Eka Robotics’ Series A.

Much of the world's physical economy still depends on people using their hands, and that work has been hard to automate because the real world is variable.

@EkaRobotics has built a Vision-Force-Action model that combines visual perception with force feedback from its robotic hands. The model, sensing, and hardware are designed together, so the robot can use physical contact itself as information.

If Eka’s approach works at scale, the implication is profound: robot experience can increasingly scale with compute rather than human labor.

Pulkit Agrawal is one of the leading researchers in robot learning and a pioneer in computational sensorimotor learning through work at his Improbable AI Lab at MIT CSAIL. Tuomas Haarnoja co-created a foundational algorithms in modern reinforcement learning at Berkeley and later worked at Google DeepMind training complex humanoid behaviors.

Congrats, @pulkitology, @haarnoja, and the Eka Robotics team!

By @stuffyokodraws and @RaghuRaghuram
